title: Göbekli Tepe Pillar 43 as a sky map of 12,500 years ago

tellings.quote: find is that that is very persuasively an astronomical diagram of the sky at the summer solstice 12 and 1/2 thousand years ago.

plain: A carved stone known as Pillar 43, at Göbekli Tepe, an ancient stone site in Turkey, is 'very persuasively an astronomical diagram of the sky at the summer solstice 12 and 1/2 thousand years ago', according to the researcher Graham Hancock. The pillar stands in a part of the site called Enclosure D, and Hancock tells Michels this without naming a source. If he is right, people were mapping the sky in detail far earlier than is usually thought.
